title: Hantavirus: How is the outbreak being contained?
facts: Three people died and several others fell ill following a hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius.
A Dutch couple who contracted hantavirus had visited a landfill site on a bird-watching tour in Ushuaia, Argentina.
The World Health Organization confirmed two deaths from the cruise ship outbreak were caused by hantavirus.
Hantavirus strains that develop into hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome have a fatality ratio of 40% to 50%.
Passengers on the MV Hondius contracted the Andes strain of hantavirus.
The Andes strain is the only hantavirus strain capable of person-to-person transmission.
Ann Rimoin serves as a professor of epidemiology at the UCLA Fielding School of Public Health.
The incubation period for hantavirus ranges between six and eight weeks.
A total of 147 people were aboard the MV Hondius during the outbreak.
The World Health Organization reported seven confirmed cases and two probable cases on the MV Hondius.
The cruise ship MV Hondius docked in Tenerife following the outbreak.
Five French nationals from the MV Hondius were placed in strict isolation after one exhibited symptoms.
The World Health Organization recommends a 42-day quarantine for high-risk contacts of confirmed hantavirus cases.
An outbreak of the Andes strain of hantavirus in Argentina in 2018-2019 killed 11 people.
Molecular biologist Kai Kupferschmidt analyzed the containment and response measures for the outbreak.
